lines: In the 2006 film version of The Devil Wears Prada, Miranda Priestly, played by Meryl Streep, scolds her unattractive assistant for imagining that high fashion doesn't affect her. Priestly explains how the deep blue color of the assistant's sweater descended over the years from fashion shows to department stores and to the **bargain** bin in which the poor girl doubtless found her garment.
在2006年电影版《穿普拉达的女王》中，梅丽尔·斯特里普饰演的米兰达·普里斯特利斥责其其貌不扬的助理，因为后者妄自以为高级时装与她无关。普里斯特利解释说，助理身上毛衣的深蓝色多年来如何从时装发布会下沉到百货商场，再下沉到特价处理箱——那个可怜姑娘无疑正是在那里买到了这件衣服。

lines: This top-down conception of the fashion business couldn't be more out of date or at odds with the feverish world described in Overdressed, Elizabeth Cline's three-year **indictment** of 'fast fashion'. In the last decade or so, advances in technology have allowed mass-market labels such as Zara, H&M, and Uniqlo to react to trends more quickly and anticipate demand more precisely. Quicker turnarounds mean less wasted inventory, more frequent releases, and more profit. These labels encourage style-conscious consumers to see clothes as **disposable** — meant to last only a wash or two, although they don't advertise that — and to renew their wardrobe every few weeks. By offering on-trend items at dirt-cheap prices, Cline argues, these brands have **hijacked** fashion cycles, shaking an industry long accustomed to a seasonal pace.

这种自上而下的时尚业观念早已过时，也与《过度着装》一书所描绘的狂热世界格格不入——该书是伊丽莎白·克莱恩历时三年对“快时尚”的控诉。近十年来，技术的进步使Zara、H&M、优衣库等大众品牌能够更迅速地回应潮流、更精准地预测需求。更快的周转意味着更少的库存浪费、更频繁的上新和更多的利润。这些品牌怂恿追逐时尚的消费者把衣服当作一次性的东西——只打算穿洗一两次，尽管它们并不如此宣传——并每隔几周就更新一遍衣橱。克莱恩认为，这些品牌以极其低廉的价格出售流行款式，劫持了时装周期，撼动了长久以来习惯按季运转的行业。

lines: Overdressed is the fashion world's answer to consumer-activist bestsellers like Michael Pollan's The Omnivore's Dilemma. 'Mass-produced clothing, like fast food, fills a hunger and need, yet is non-durable and wasteful,' Cline argues. Americans, she finds, buy roughly 20 **billion** garments a year — about 64 items per person — and no matter how much they give away, this excess leads to waste.

lines: Towards the end of Overdressed, Cline introduced her ideal, a Brooklyn woman named Sarah Kate Beaumont, who since 2008 has made all of her own clothes — and beautifully. But as Cline is the first to note, it took Beaumont decades to perfect her **craft**; her example can't be knocked off.

lines: Though several fast-fashion companies have made efforts to curb their impact on labor and the environment — including H&M, with its green Conscious Collection line — Cline believes lasting change can only be effected by the customer. She exhibits the **idealism** common to many advocates of sustainability, be it in food or in energy. Vanity is a constant; people will only start shopping more sustainably when they can't afford not to.
尽管几家快时尚公司已努力遏制其对劳工和环境的影响——包括H&M及其绿色的“自觉系列”产品线——克莱恩相信，持久的改变只能由消费者来实现。她展现出许多可持续发展倡导者共有的理想主义，无论在食品还是能源领域。虚荣心是永恒的；只有当人们不这样购物就负担不起时，他们才会开始更可持续地消费。

lines: An old saying has it that half of all advertising budgets are wasted — the trouble is, no one knows which half. In the internet age, at least in theory, this fraction can be much reduced. By watching what people search for, click on and say online, companies can aim 'behavioural' ads at those most likely to buy.
一句老话说得好：广告预算有一半都打了水漂——问题在于，没人知道是哪一半。而在互联网时代，至少在理论上，这一比例可以大大降低。通过观察人们在网上的搜索、点击和言论，公司可以把“行为”广告精准投放到最有可能购买的人群。

lines: In December 2010 America's Federal Trade Commission (FTC) proposed adding a 'do not track' (DNT) option to internet browsers, so that users could tell advertisers that they did not want to be followed. Microsoft's Internet Explorer and Apple's Safari both offer DNT; Google's Chrome is due to do so this year. In February the FTC and the Digital Advertising Alliance (DAA) agreed that the industry would get **cracking** on responding to DNT requests.
2010年12月，美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）提议在互联网浏览器中增加“禁止跟踪”（DNT）选项，让用户可以告知广告主自己不愿被跟踪。微软的IE浏览器和苹果的Safari均已提供DNT；谷歌的Chrome预计今年跟进。今年2月，FTC与数字广告联盟（DAA）达成一致：浏览器行业将着手响应DNT请求。

lines: Advertisers are horrified. Human nature being what it is, most people stick with default settings. Few switch DNT on now, but if tracking is off it will stay off. Bob Liodice, the chief executive of the Association of National Advertisers, says consumers will be worse off if the industry cannot collect information about their preferences. People will not get fewer ads, he says. 'They'll get less meaningful, less targeted ads.'

lines: Perhaps willfully, it may be easier to think about such lengthy timescales than about the more immediate future. The potential **evolution** of today's technology, and its social consequences, is dazzlingly complicated, and it's perhaps best left to science fiction writers and futurologists to explore the many possibilities we can envisage. That's one reason why we have launched Arc, a new publication dedicated to the near future.

lines: The trick is to direct these funds better. The European Union Framework funding programs have long had a category specifically targeted at social scientists. lines: One of these urges has to do with creating a state of peace in the midst of turbulence, a 'still point of the turning world,' to borrow a phrase from T. S. Eliot. (47) A sacred place of peace, however crude it may be, is a distinctly human need, as opposed to shelter, which is a distinctly animal need. This distinction is so much so that where the latter is lacking, as it is for these unlikely gardeners, the former becomes all the more urgent. 这些冲动之一，关乎在纷乱中营造一种安宁之境——借用T.S.艾略特的话说，是“旋转世界中的静止之点”。(47) 一处神圣的安宁之地，无论多么简陋，都是一种鲜明的人类需求，而栖身之所则是一种鲜明的动物性需求。这一区分意义重大：在栖身之所匮乏的地方——正如这些难以归类的园丁的处境——前一种需求便愈发迫切。从容是一种心境，它借由理顺个人与环境的关系而成为可能。(48) 无家可归者的花园，实际上是没有家园的花园，它们把“形式”引入一种原本不存在形式、或者说形式无从辨认的城市环境之中。由此，它们为它们所立足的那部分难以言表的环境赋予了从容的气息。

lines: Another urge or need that these gardens appear to respond to, or to arise from, is so intrinsic that we are barely ever conscious of its abiding claims on us. When we are deprived of green, of plants, of trees, (49) most of us give in to a demoralization of spirit which we usually blame on some psychological conditions, until one day we find ourselves in a garden and feel the oppression vanish as if by magic. In most of the homeless gardens of New York City the actual cultivation of plants is unfeasible, yet even so the compositions often seem to represent attempts to call forth the spirit of plant and animal life, if only symbolically, through a clump-like arrangement of materials, an introduction of colors, small pools of water, and a frequent presence of petals or leaves as well as of stuffed animals. On display here are various fantasy elements whose reference, at some basic level, seems to be the natural world. (50) It is this implicit or explicit reference to nature that fully justifies the use of the word garden, though in a 'liberated' sense, to describe these synthetic constructions. In them we can see biophilia — a yearning for contact with nonhuman life — assuming uncanny representational forms.

这些花园似乎在回应、或者说源自另一种冲动或需求，它如此根植于本性，以至于我们几乎意识不到它对我们经久不歇的召唤。当我们被剥夺了绿色、植物和树木时，(49) 我们中的大多数人会陷入一种精神萎靡的状态，而我们通常把这种状态归咎于某些心理原因，直到有一天我们置身于花园之中，才感到那种压抑如魔法般消散。在纽约市大多数无家可归者的花园里，真正栽种植物并不现实，但即便如此，这些布局往往像是力图唤起动植物生命的神韵——哪怕只是象征性的——其手段包括把材料堆成团状、引入色彩、设置小水池，以及常常陈设花瓣、树叶乃至毛绒动物。这里展示着种种幻想元素，它们在某种基本层面上所指涉的，似乎正是自然界。(50) 正是这种对自然的或隐或显的指涉，充分证明了用“花园”一词——尽管是从其“被解放”的意义上——来描述这些人造构造物是恰当的。在它们之中，我们可以看到亲生命性——即与非人类生命接触的渴望——呈现出令人称奇的表现形式。

data.image_desc: 图画中，一群大学毕业生站在人生的岔路口，面前延伸出四条道路，路标上分别写着'求职''考研''出国''创业'，毕业生们面露迷茫、犹豫不决，图画下方写着'选择'二字。（原文PDF图片缺失，此描述据真题补齐）
sample: As is vividly depicted in the drawing, a group of college graduates are standing at a crossroads of life. Four roads stretch ahead of them, marked respectively with signs reading 'job-hunting', 'postgraduate entrance examination', 'studying abroad' and 'starting a business'. Puzzled and hesitant, they have no idea which path to take, while the word 'choice' below the picture drives home its theme.
正如图画生动描绘的那样，一群大学毕业生正站在人生的岔路口。四条道路在他们面前延伸，路标上分别写着“求职”“考研”“出国”和“创业”。他们一脸茫然、犹豫不决，不知该走哪条路，而图画下方的“选择”二字则点明了主题。

sample: The implied meaning of the picture is profound: on the eve of graduation, young people are confronted with a variety of life choices, and none of them can be avoided or postponed. Each road represents a different future, with its own opportunities and risks. What makes the decision so agonizing is not the lack of options but their abundance — the fear of missing out on the alternatives often leaves graduates wavering between paths.
这幅画的寓意深刻：毕业前夕，年轻人面临着多种多样的人生抉择，而且谁也无法回避或推迟。每条道路都代表着不同的未来，各有其机遇与风险。令抉择如此煎熬的并非无路可选，而是选择太多——对错失其他可能性的担忧，常使毕业生在各条道路之间摇摆不定。

sample: In my view, there is no absolutely right or wrong choice; what truly matters is to know oneself and to follow one's inner voice. A wise graduate should take into account his own interest, ability and long-term goal rather than blindly follow the crowd. Once a decision is made, one should march forward with determination and never look back, for it is persistent effort, not the choice itself, that ultimately decides how far we can go.
在我看来，选择本无绝对的对错之分；真正重要的是认识自己、听从内心的声音。明智的毕业生应综合考虑自身的兴趣、能力和长远目标，而不是盲目随大流。一旦作出决定，就应坚定前行、绝不回头，因为最终决定我们能走多远的，是持之以恒的努力，而非选择本身。
